tone_statements.quote: 第二，古浊上的口语字在韶州片土话中有三种声调类型：第一是梅村、桂头独立为阳上调，这是最原始的一种类型；第二是白沙、周田、上窑、腊石和犁市今读阴去，这种类型显然是第一种类型演变来的，与东江流域的“本地话”以及南雄乌迳话相同；第三种类型是石陂、石塘、长来、北乡今读去声（阴、阳去不分），这种类型显然是第二种类型演变来的。 [...] 古浊上的白读层今读去声实际上有两种小类：一是如东源县骆湖镇的“本地话”和韶关浈江区石陂土话、仁化县石塘土话，古浊上的白读层与阴去合并为去声，浊去并入阴平，表面上看只有一个去声，但本质上保留了阴去的底层调，与上述古浊上的白读层今读阴去的类型相同；
tone_statements.translation: Second, colloquial words with MC voiced-rising tone show three tonal types in the Shaozhou-group Tuhua: first, in Meicun and Guitou they form an independent yang-shang tone, the most archaic type; second, in Baisha, Zhoutian, Shangyao, Lashi and Lishi they are now read yin-qu, a type evidently developed from the first and identical to the 'bendihua' of the Dongjiang basin and to Nanxiong Wujing; the third type is Shibei, Shitang, Changlai and Beixiang, where they are now read qu tone (yin-qu and yang-qu not distinguished), evidently developed from the second type. [...] The type 'colloquial voiced-rising now read qu' actually has two subtypes: one, as in the bendihua of Luohu town (Dongyuan county) and the Shibei Tuhua of Zhenjiang district, Shaoguan, and the Shitang Tuhua of Renhua county, where the colloquial voiced-rising layer merged with yin-qu into (one) qu tone and voiced-qu went into yin-ping, so that on the surface there is only one qu tone but underlyingly the yin-qu category is preserved, the same as the 'read yin-qu' type above;

sources.note: Uses tone-category development as the criterion for subgrouping Guangdong Hakka and argues the Shaozhou Tuhua (incl. Shibei) belong with 'Old Hakka'. For Shibei Tuhua specifically: the colloquial layer of MC voiced-rising (浊上) words has merged with yin-qu into a single qu tone and MC voiced-qu (浊去) has gone to yin-ping, so the variety has on the surface only one qu tone while preserving the underlying yin-qu category (惠韶型, second historical layer, grouped with 石塘); MC voiced obstruents are aspirated regardless of tone in Shibei. sources.tag: read: notes on tone
sources.note: Sinitic tone categories presupposed; only diminutive changed tones (Shibei 33/3; Dacun 2ʔ23, 4ʔ45 rising, glottalised) and entering tones (yin 5, yang 3, glottal-final) given; no inventory or count.

tone.quote: 合变式中 ,合变式 1 一般只有 1 个读音 ,唯有石陂有 3 和 33 两个读音 。石陂中古四声八类的字发生变调之后无论声母的清浊调值一般都是 33。读变音 3 的只限于来自清声母的入声字 … 总之 ,石陂变音 3 不是因为声母清浊的不同而产生的 , 而是由于声调的不同而导致的 ,应该是小称变音 33 的变异 … 同样 ,为了保持这个声调格局 ,石陂中塞式的小称变音便只能直接舒化 ,而不经历后塞的阶段 ,因为该方言中的入声仍分阴阳 ,且都读后塞式 。
tone.locator: p. 112 (text below 表2, both columns) to p. 113, sec. 一(二); and p. 115 col. 2, sec. 二(二)3
tone.translation: In the merged type, type 1 generally has one reading; only Shibei has two, 3 and 33. In Shibei, syllables of all eight MC tone classes, once changed, generally read 33 regardless of initial voicing. Changed tone 3 is limited to entering-tone syllables from voiceless initials … In short, Shibei's changed tone 3 arises not from initial voicing but from tone, and should be a variant of the diminutive changed tone 33 … Likewise, to keep this tonal pattern, Shibei's mid-glottal diminutive changed tone could only de-check directly, with no final-glottal stage, because its entering tone still splits yin/yang, both read glottal-final.
tone.summary: Sinitic tone categories presupposed; only diminutive changed tones (Shibei 33/3; Dacun 2ʔ23, 4ʔ45 rising, glottalised) and entering tones (yin 5, yang 3, glottal-final) given; no inventory or count.
